# Lessons from keel

<!-- Generated by keel (practice lessons) from keel's catalogue; keel update rewrites it. Never edit it by hand: add this project's own lessons to docs/reviews/lessons.md. -->

Failure shapes keel has learned across its projects, each with what it cost
and the guard that caught it. Numbers and provenance are keel's catalogue's.
A row with an empty *Where* applies to every project; a tagged row only to
projects with that stack. Read this beside the project's own table
(`docs/reviews/lessons.md`) before adding a guard: the shape is usually already here.

This project's stack (`stack` in `.keel/keel.json`): `node`, `web`, `gcp`, `github-actions`. 57 of keel's lessons apply: every universal one, and those tagged for this stack.

| # | The shape of it | What it cost | Guard | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **A copied practice ages, and can't hear that the original changed.** Every hand-port of a skill or an AGENTS.md section is a fork with no upstream. *(keel, observed 2026-10-02)* | isocan kept an untracked second copy of its conduct skill under `.agents/skills/`, dated 20 Sep. By 2 Oct it was missing a week of changes to the real one in `.claude/skills/`, including `7227f325`. A reader of the wrong copy would have run the expensive version. Across the fleet, duo, cajones and ledger each carry a different hand-port of the same phase practice. | One file, many doorways: a skill lives once, under `.agents/skills/`, and `.claude/skills/` is a symlink. Adapted files pin their `source` commit. *Planned:* `keel doctor` reports second copies and drift (phase 5), and `keel learn` polls sources (phase 8). | |
| 2 | **Status written in more than one place drifts, and both copies look authoritative.** *(ledger 6, duo 1, cajones)* | In ledger, the README said phase 2 was complete while SPEC.md said phase 4 was built. Both had been hand-edited the same day. | Status lives in each phase's front matter. `docs/ROADMAP.md` is derived from it, and `npm run roadmap:check` fails CI when the roadmap is stale, a claim lacks evidence, or a dependency loops. *Implemented on keel* (phase 0). | |
| 3 | **A guard that fires into a room nobody is in.** *(ledger 8, duo 2)* | CI was red on three consecutive commits and production served an eight-hour-old build. Both were found by accident. | Every nightly and deploy check fails as a *workflow*, which GitHub emails about. It is never only a page. *Planned:* phase 10 asserts it. | |
| 4 | **A green subset hides a red suite.** `npm test \| tail` reports tail's exit code, and a fast lane leaves out the files a change broke. *(isocan house rules, conduct)* | In isocan, a green subset hid a real failure three times in one week. Each time the failure was in a file the change didn't name. A subagent reported "suite passed" while six tests failed. | The conductor reads exit codes, not tails, and runs the whole check once on the integrated tree before landing. *Implemented* in the conduct skill. | |
| 5 | **Verification repeated at every level costs more than it catches.** *(isocan `7227f325`)* | In one conducted session, builders ran the whole suite 53 times (2.8 hours, a quarter of all subagent time) and typecheck 56 times. The conductor's own deep run then repeated all of it. | Builders test the files they touched. The conductor runs the full check once, detached. Briefs point to docs rather than paste them, and stay under 600 words. *Implemented* in the conduct skill. *Planned:* the cost is measured by `keel improve` (phase 11). | |
| 6 | **A grader that reports zeros when it breaks is believed.** *(isocan evals, lesson 8 there)* | isocan's first grader scored a stretched image 8/8, because its probe threw and every reading fell to empty. | A self-test on a fixture built to fail must fail every check before a run counts. An instrument that can't run exits non-zero. *Planned:* phase 11. | |
| 7 | **A guard that stores a copy of a fact instead of deriving it.** *(ledger 12)* | ledger's CI hard-coded "install web/ only". When the fact changed, the copy became wrong in both directions and the comment defended it. | Read the single statement of the fact (the deploy config, the practice manifest) in the test, never restate it. Keel's version of this is `practice.json` (phase 1). | |
| 8 | **A fake that mirrors the implementation can only confirm it.** *(ledger 11)* | ledger's fake Gmail matched labels by id, exactly as the buggy code did. The tidy-up found nothing for weeks and reported success. | Fakes model the third party's real behaviour. Keel stubs `gh` at the boundary, with recorded real responses. | |
| 9 | **Machine pull requests pile up without a drain.** *(isocan night shift)* | Five open machine PRs at once in isocan on 9 Sep 2026. Each was waiting on a person to remember it. | A workflow's queue holds at most one open PR, the newest, and the run drains its predecessors itself. *Planned:* phase 10. | |
| 10 | **A commit step that can't see a first-time file.** `git diff --quiet` compares against the index, so a newly created file reads as no change. *(ledger audit workflow)* | ledger's audit agent lost every report it had ever written. An empty report is what a healthy audit looks like, so nothing seemed wrong. | Workflows test `git status --porcelain`, and push with a rebase-and-retry loop. In local gates, the conductor runs `git add -N` on new files before checks that use `git ls-files` (isocan lesson 70). *Planned:* phase 10's workflow test. | |
| 11 | **A check that dispatches events proves the handler, not that a person can reach it.** *(duo 4)* | 25 duo examples shipped "verified" in poses where no real tap could reach them. | Where a person's input matters, drive real input (CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`) and say so in the evidence. Per kind, not fleet-wide. | web |
| 12 | **A tool built for one version of a service, silently incompatible with the next.** *(duo 3)* | duo's `isocan` CLI couldn't create a canvas on the hosted home, and `upgrade` refused to help. | When a CLI talks to something versioned, check the other side's version first. For keel this means `keel update` updates the CLI before it runs any migration (phase 6). | |
| 13 | **A tool that restores its own copy erases the edit it should have reported.** A renderer that makes the tree match its template is "correct" every time it runs, and each run deletes the one piece of evidence that someone needed it to be different. *(keel, phase 5)* | `keel render` silently overwrote a project's edit to a managed file. Phase 1's own tests asserted this as the right behaviour ("a second render restores managed files"). It was found only when phase 5's builder asked what render does to a file that doctor calls `edited`. | `render` refuses to write over an `edited` or `both` target (exit 1, nothing written) and points at `keel doctor --fix restore\|eject`. `tests/doctor.test.mjs` asserts the refusal for a file and for a block. | |
| 14 | **A check spawned from inside a test runner inherits the runner's context and passes while running nothing. What the parent sets for itself (a runner's marker variable, the machine's global config) reaches the child, which then does something other than what the test meant and still exits 0.** *(keel, phase 6)* | Every keel test that spawned a project's own `npm run check` (init, adopt, practices) had been green while measuring nothing since phase 1. A test file that only throws exited 0. Found by phase 6's builder, when its gate assertion passed although the project's tests had been deleted. | All spawns go through `tests/helpers/run.mjs`, which strips `NODE_TEST_*`. Every spawned gate also asserts that tests ran and names one. `tests/helpers.test.mjs` fails on a failing child that exits 0, and on any raw spawn in a test file. `keel update` strips the same variables before it runs a project's check. The same shape came from the developer's machine on 4 October: a global `core.fsmonitor=true` failed 31 tests in one session's sandbox. Under a hostile config (fsmonitor and commit signing on, no name), 59 failed even with fsmonitor pinned off. `tests/helpers/hermetic.mjs`, loaded before every test, now isolates git config (an empty global, no system config, a synthetic identity), and `tests/hermetic.test.mjs` fails if it's ever dropped. | |
| 15 | **A version gate decides who gets a fix, and anyone who arrives after the version never gets it.** "Apply what's newer than you" assumes every project started at the beginning. *(keel, phase 6)* | Migration 0001 (`to: 0.1.0`) could never run on ritmo: adopt stamps the current practice, so a project adopted at 0.1.0 is "already on 0.1.0". Every test passed, because the fixtures started at 0.0.0. Found on a walk against a fresh clone of the real project. | Migrations run when `applies()` is true and aren't yet recorded in the project's `migrations` list. Version comparison stays only for "update keel first". A test adopts at the current version and asserts 0001 runs. | |
| 16 | **A doc that restates what the code knows goes stale silently.** A README verb table, a feature list or a "planned" label is a hand-kept copy of a fact the code owns. Nothing fails when the two part ways, so the doc keeps saying the old thing in a confident voice. *(keel, observed 2026-10-03; ledger 6 and 12 are the same shape)* | keel's README called every verb "planned" through eight phases that built them, and was missing `drain`, `phase`, `render` and `fleet update`. The agent guide stayed current over the same eight phases, because a test reads the verb registry against it. The README had no such test. The owner found it by asking whether a README explained keel. | `tests/docs.test.mjs` (phase 18) reads the live verb registry and the `practices/` directory and fails when the README's verb and practice tables miss one, list one that doesn't exist, or call a built verb "planned". Conduct's Record step asks "does this change what a person or an agent is told?" and updates README and the agent guide in the same commit. "Remember to update the docs" is not a guard. On its first run the test found `base` missing from the practices table, in the README rewritten by hand that morning. | |
| 17 | **A test whose injected value doesn't reach every path is green only while the real value happens to match. The test sets a value in-process, but a path it reaches (a spawned process, a file read from disk, a live service) reads the real one, and nobody notices while the two agree.** *(keel, v0.3.1)* | Cutting v0.3.1 turned CI red on the release commit itself: one fixture project became "behind". The release step hadn't run the gate, and the conductor ran the check *before* releasing, not after. CI was the first reader. | Fleet verbs take the version through `KEEL_FLEET_PRACTICE` in tests, so the spawned CLI gets it too. A regression test injects versions far above and far below the live one. `keel release` now runs the project's gate after the bump and before committing; on red it restores every file and makes no commit and no tag. The same shape came back the next day with the live *world* instead of the live version: a CLI test ran `fleet update` against the real `fleet.json` through real GitHub, and went red the moment ledger was really adopted. Tests that run `fleet`, `lessons` or `learn` must now set `KEEL_GH`; the run helper throws without it, and a source guard fails any test file that forgets. | |
| 18 | **A gate that passes on a tree it does not commit.** The run checks its working copy, then commits a fixed list of paths. Anything a step rewrote outside that list passed the gate and never left the runner. *(ledger, phase 14)* | The first real Loop cycle on ledger (#23) pulled 10 findings. `afterRender` regenerated `docs/ROADMAP.md`, which counts findings, and the gate passed on that tree. The PR carried only `docs/loop/` and `docs/LOOP.md`, and the drain merged it as data. ledger's main went red on its next push: the roadmap check failed on a count that was 10 short. The phase's own note recorded the cycle as a success. | `"loop" "afterRenderWrites"` names what `afterRender` writes. The workflow's config step turns it into the exact paths it stages (`git add -- $PATHS`), and the drain counts the same files as `keel-loop/` data (`extraData`). `tests/loop.test.mjs` runs the config step itself, fails on a fixed `git add docs/loop docs/LOOP.md`, and checks that the three copies of the path rule agree. A machine PR's staged paths come from the same config as its gate's writes, never from a list typed into the workflow. | |
| 19 | **A value that looks absolute (a day, a formatted string, a path) is relative to the machine, zone or moment that produced it.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Records written on one host or zone read wrong on another, and the error is invisible where it was written. | Values crossing a boundary carry their context (offset, normalisation, explicit path); tests run under a second zone or host. | |
| 20 | **A setting held at a third party switches a feature off, and nothing you own logs anything.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | A feature is dead for days while tests, deploys and logs stay green; someone using it finds out. | Pin the setting where possible; otherwise check it before relying on it, report into a room someone is in, and prefer the sturdier credential. | |
| 21 | **A mitigation that reduces the work but not the thing actually rationed.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | The quota runs out while the fix meant to prevent it sits in place, measuring the wrong number. | Before trusting a mitigation, check that the number it moves is the number with the limit. | |
| 22 | **Views are filters: an item that no view selects is invisible without being gone.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | New items drop out of sight on the very screen where they were entered, unnoticed until counted. | A property test that every item lands in at least one view, or a remainder view that catches the rest. | |
| 23 | **A timeout sized for the code path, then spent by a person in the middle of it.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Expiries and flushes fire mid-task, presenting as hangs or as batching that never batches. | Size limits against the human act, and assert in a test that the limit covers realistic human time. | |
| 24 | **A correct fallback hides that the fast path never runs; a cache that never hits looks like one that works.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Something ships slow on every request with right answers, so nothing fails. | Test that the fast path is reached (the artifact is deployed; the cache revalidates and serves a 304), and log durations. | |
| 25 | **A test fixture pins a real date that the code compares with now.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Main goes red later, on a commit that touched nothing. | CI re-runs the suite with the clock moved a year forward; fixtures use dates relative to today, or the clock is injected. | |
| 26 | **Missing data coerced to a valid empty value, and "unchanged" answered without checking the copy is complete.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Empty records parse as real ones and crash far from the cause; lost data is never re-sent. | Missing means missing: skip or fail. Answer "unchanged" only after checking the copy is complete. | |
| 27 | **An editor reads part of a record and writes what it read back as the whole.** *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Every save, even untouched, silently drops the parts the editor did not show. | Saving an untouched record must reproduce it byte for byte; refuse a write that drops content nobody removed. | |
| 28 | **What you test is not what people get.** A checkout has every file; the package a stranger installs is built by a step (npm pack, a deploy's install) that drops, renames or adds files on its own rules. *(keel, 4 Oct; ledger 2 is the deploy-side twin)* | `npx github:dalmaer/keel init` failed for everyone from the day keel went public: npm strips every `.gitignore` when it packs a package, git installs included, so the `base` practice's template never shipped. All 258 tests passed against the checkout. Found by a fresh agent told to use only the documented `npx` route. | The template is `files/gitignore`, and `package.json` `files` lists what ships. `tests/package.test.mjs` runs `npm pack`, unpacks, checks every practice template is inside, and runs `init` from the unpacked copy to a passing project gate. | |
| 29 | **A run that finishes is reported as succeeding: the verdict comes from reaching the end, not from checking the result.** *(dalmaer/cajones)* | People are told they did well when nothing worked, and dashboards count empty or cancelled runs as passes; the message carries no error, so it is believed. | Derive success from the measured result; test a run with no input and a cancelled run and assert neither reports success. Finished and succeeded are separate states. | |
| 30 | **Code inside another language's string is checked by neither.** A Node script in a single-quoted shell string, in a YAML `run:` block: YAML parses, the tests read the YAML as text, and nothing runs the shell or the script until the workflow does. *(keel, 4 Oct)* | An apostrophe in a comment ("the secret's NAME", "project's afterRender") closed the shell string. ledger's scheduled Loop run failed on 4 Oct, and its first 0.6.3 night failed at "Read the config". Every keel test passed, because they read the workflows as text. | `tests/workflows.test.mjs` extracts every `run:` block from every shipped and rendered workflow, runs `bash -n` on it (with `${{ }}` replaced), and runs `node --check` on every inline `node -e '…'` body. It fails on the pre-fix files exactly where GitHub did. | |
| 31 | **A machine edits another owner's copy.** A file one tool owns is also in another tool's reach: Renovate updates every workflow it can see, including the ones keel manages, so the project's copy moves before keel's template does. *(keel, 5 Oct; duo)* | duo's Actions-major PR bumped keel-night.yml to v7 a day before keel's own Renovate bumped the template; the file read as the project's own change (`both`), and every later update would have been refused. | Drift is settled three ways before it is called the project's: laid over the template keel wrote (found by the lock's practice version in keel's tags, checked against the lock's hash), an edit that gives exactly keel's template today is `behind`, and update takes it. `tests/doctor.test.mjs` ("a change keel has since made too"), with mutations. | |
| 32 | **A write lands on a target nobody checked.** Found by proximity (the working directory, the nearest marker, a default path) or by a name nobody looked up, it is right only while there is one candidate. *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Once code and data split, writes landed where nothing committed or read them; a new file written over an existing name deleted its content without an error. | Every writer checks an identity marker on its target before its first write; creating a file first checks that the name is free. | |
| 33 | **A rule written without the precedence of the system it lives in.** A catch-all route, a fallback handler or a hidden state is declared correctly and loses to something stronger: an earlier route, a framework default, an animation driving the same property. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Requests reached the wrong handler; a state declared hidden showed all the time; every test passed because each tested the rule alone. | Test the rule against every other rule the system already applies to the same input; prefer an allowlist to a catch-all. | |
| 34 | **A check guards one door of several.** Access or visibility is enforced on the usual route, while a combined view, another spelling of the path or a second entrance serves the same thing. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Content refused at the normal route was reachable through a list, a batch or an alternate URL. | Enforce on the item served, not the route asked for; a test lists every entrance and compares each with the normal one. | |
| 35 | **Caught is not kept.** An optimistic change clears what a person typed before the save confirms; the failure is caught and reported, and the words are gone. *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Typed text lost whenever a save failed, in every place that shared the pattern. | Every optimistic change carries an undo that the failure path runs, without overwriting anything typed since; a test fails the save and checks the input came back. | web |
| 36 | **A verifier waits for an exact version instead of the change it contains.** Deploys keep moving, so the wait runs out on a version already replaced, and running out is not reported as a failure. *(dalmaer/ledger)* | Much of CI's time spent on waits that could never succeed, ending green. | Accept the expected version or a descendant of it, check that a deploy actually ran before waiting, and fail loudly when production never arrives. | |
| 37 | **A test written for the reported reproduction, not the invariant.** It stays green when the same bug returns another way: the other axis, another copy of the rule, an input where it usually is not. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Fixes guarded only for the case someone happened to report; the bug came back through a sibling. | State the invariant once and loop it over every axis or copy; break the fix several ways before believing the test. | |
| 38 | **A check that never evaluates its claim.** It fails before its assertion, matches a relative by substring, mutates a value into itself, or lives on a branch that never merged; its green or red says nothing about its subject. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Guards counted as protection that protected nothing. | Confirm a failure happens at the assertion, match exactly, assert that a mutation changed the value, and check that the guard runs on the trunk. | |
| 39 | **Work a test starts outlives the test.** A spawned process, a fire-and-forget writer or an open handle is stopped on the happy path only, and its failure lands on whichever test runs next. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | One cause read as random flakes in unrelated files; reruns taught people to ignore red. | Everything a test starts goes on a list its teardown drains and awaits; a test checks that nothing changes after close resolves. | |
| 40 | **A wait whose deadline nobody measured.** A library default, a tick count, a timer the platform rounds, a line that is not the last of its sequence, or a shared limit raised for the one case that complained. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Tests that fail only under load or in the full parallel suite, often as a wrong value; limits that keep growing. | Wait on the condition itself with an explicit deadline and message; measure the distribution before setting a limit; reproduce by slowing one thing down, alone and in the full suite. | |
| 41 | **A lock that does not match the state it protects.** Held in one process while writers live in several, or scoped wider than its state so a slow call inside it stalls every writer. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Fields lost silently between concurrent writers; every write stalled behind one network wait. | Key the lock to the state and make every writer honour it; one test runs two real writers, another holds a slow call open while an unrelated write must land. | |
| 42 | **A check and its use happen at different moments.** A file checked and then rewritten before use, a snapshot and a log cursor taken apart, two callers racing for one recovery, an absence asserted over an object others are using. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Content used that was never checked; windows that neither read covers; flaky reds blamed on the test. | Keep the checked bytes through use, take related reads together, and scope an assertion to the caller it is about. | |
| 43 | **A value computed once is trusted after its inputs change.** Derived at creation, loaded at startup, or cached by the very process asking whether it is stale. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Stale output that looked like an old bug returning; a frozen client confirmed healthy; a running host kept its old wiring. | One re-derive path that every writer of an input calls; staleness read from a store other writers write; after a config change, verify what the running process actually loaded. | |
| 44 | **Nothing bounds the stuck case.** A retry budget checked between attempts cannot stop one attempt that hangs; a loop whose only exit is a helper's side effect turns a bug into a hang. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Stalls far past the budget, and runs that never finish and leave nothing to read. | Put the deadline on the attempt itself; treat a hang as a finding, and test the helper's contract below the loop. | |
| 45 | **A guard that asserts the mechanism instead of the property.** It forbids a simpler implementation that keeps the property, so the mechanism becomes mandatory. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | A slow or awkward implementation outlived its reason because a test demanded it. | Ask of every assertion what it forbids; if it forbids a simpler version that keeps the property, rewrite it to the property. | |
| 46 | **Reading the code cannot find a performance bug.** A hypothesis formed by reading is confident and wrong; the profiler finds where the time goes. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Time spent optimising code that was not the cost. | When the symptom is slow, measure and profile before forming a hypothesis; keep a change only when the measurement moves beyond its noise. | |
| 47 | **A condition nested inside an unrelated one inherits its answer.** Two conditions, each correct alone, are wrong together when one sits inside the other. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Behaviour that changed when an unrelated setting changed. | Give each condition its own name and line; test each with the other both ways. | |
| 48 | **An identity built from the wrong parts.** A key finer than what is displayed lets duplicates through; a key joined with a separator collides when a field contains it. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Duplicates on screen; two different records sharing one entry. | Every filter feeding a list uses the list's own identity; tuples are encoded unambiguously, and the record returned is checked against the tuple asked for. | |
| 49 | **CI that runs only on the trunk makes the trunk the first place a failure shows.** Review without a run lets red land first. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | The trunk went red and held back everything it feeds, deploys included. | Run the gate on every pull request; keel's ci practice does. | |
| 50 | **A checker's scope is a claim nobody stated.** Left unset, it walks worktrees, build output and other checkouts. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Slow runs, results counted from other trees, overflowing output read as a broken instrument; keel's own tests copied an agent's worktree (6 Oct). | State what each checker walks and assert it both ways: it reads what it must and nothing else. keel ignores .claude/worktrees/. | |
| 51 | **Advice is not the decision.** A handoff that carries an agent's recommendation but not the person's choice makes the next agent act against what the person chose. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Work done in the direction the person had declined. | Record the person's choice apart from the advice; test by choosing against the advice and checking the next step follows the choice. | |
| 52 | **A file declared generated whose generator does not rewrite it whole.** Merges trust the generator to settle it, and content from the other side vanishes. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Merged content dropped silently, exit 0. | A test appends a marker to each declared file, runs the generator, and fails if the marker survives. | |
| 53 | **A fake secret shaped like a real one.** Scanners cannot tell them apart, so every fixture is a leak alert someone must disprove. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | False leak alerts, each costing a person's time. | Fakes say fake in their value; a test fails on real-shaped secrets in tracked files. | |
| 54 | **A deliberate break made in the shared checkout.** A mutation or probe edited in the tree a builder or another session is using gets lost, committed, or tested by someone else. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | A builder's change dropped by a checkout; probes left behind in the working tree. | conduct: deliberate breaks run in a temp copy or a separate git worktree, never the shared checkout. | |
| 55 | **A guard cell that names something nothing runs.** The lessons table claims protection that a habit or a person provides. *(dglazkov/isocan)* | Rows read as guarded that a later change could break with nothing going red. | lessons: a Guard names only something an automated run invokes; anything else is marked planned or habit. | |
| 56 | **A test asserts what holds only for most random draws.** Its fixture draws something random (an id, a uuid, a port, a time) and the assertion is true for nearly every draw but not all: a fixed four-character prefix of a hash over random ids is usually unique. *(keel, 6 Oct)* | Passes locally hundreds of times, fails on CI once, does not reproduce, and reads as a flake in unrelated code; the product was right all along. | The test derives what it asserts from the same draw (the shortest prefix that is unique among this run's ids), and prints the draw when it fails. `tests/loose-ends.test.mjs` ("marks persist across runs"). | |
| 57 | **A parallel suite waits for its longest file.** A runner that starts many test files at once but runs each file's tests one after another can finish no sooner than its slowest file, however many cores it has. One file of 29 tests took 96 s, about twice the rest of the suite. *(keel, 9 Oct)* | Every gate paid the one file's time: `npm test` ran 96 s where splitting the file gave 47–51 s; running files longest first gave nothing more. | Planned: phase 57's `critical_file` measure names a file whose own time sets the suite's, and proposes splitting it. | |
